item.title: EUBAM Rafah - Vacancy Announcement – Various positions (4 posts)
item.description: The European Union Border Assistance Mission for the Rafah Crossing Point – code name EUBAM Rafah – was launched on 24 November 2005 to monitor the operations of the border crossing point between the Gaza Strip and Egypt, after Israel and the Palestinian Authority concluded an Agreement on Movement and Access on 15 November 2005. The Council of the European Union approved that the EU should undertake the third-party role proposed. EUBAM Rafah is currently seeking dynamic, highly skilled candidates for immediate recruitment to fill the following Four (4) vacancies: SECL 01 Mission Security Assistant (1 post): main responsibilities are related to providing security and operational support to Mission staff, monitoring the security situation, and supporting security procedures, risk assessments and travel arrangements. HRL 02 Human Resources Officer (1 post): main responsibilities are related to recruitment, staff administration, training, HR records and systems, and supporting payroll and other HR-related processes. HRL 03 Human Resources Assistant/Travel (1 post): main responsibilities are related to coordinating official travel and entitlements, maintaining HR and travel records, and providing administrative support to the HR Office. HoML 02 Protocol/Administrative Officer (1 post): main responsibilities are related to protocol, liaison and administrative support to the Head of Mission and Deputy Head of Mission, including official visits, events and coordination with external stakeholders. Employment regime: Locally Contracted Staff hired under Israeli Local Labor Law Duty Station: Ramat Gan - Tel Aviv Opening Date: 01 October 2026 Closing Date: 23 October 2026 General employment/eligibility requirements: Education and professional experience, as well as proficiency in English, Arabic and Hebrew, as specified in the relevant Job Description; a valid identification document permitting employment and unrestricted movement within the Mission’s area of operations; medical fitness for work; and a clean criminal record. IMPORTANT: Work is expected to be performed physically at the Mission offices in Ramat Gan, Monday through Friday. Candidates must be able to make the necessary arrangements to travel to and from the office premises on a daily basis. Applicants must hold a valid local identification document or work permit authorising employment at the Mission. IMPORTANT INFORMATION FOR THE APPLICANTS Applicants are reminded that the work of the Selection Committee is strictly confidential. Therefore, applicants must not contact, either directly or indirectly, any member of the Selection Committee, nor request that any other person do so on their behalf. item.title: EEAS Call for Expression of Interest for the recruitment of one Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) as Administrative Assistant (AST2) SG Office – Office of the Secretary General
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The SG Office supports the Secretary-General in her leadership and overall coordination of the EEAS, ensuring coherence across the Service and alignment with institutional priorities, in close liaison with the Cabinet of the HR/VP. It provides support to the Secretary General including the preparation, coordination, and follow-up of the Secretary-General’s engagements and decision-making. The SG Office manages the Secretary-General’s schedule, coordinates briefings, decisions, and follow-up actions, and ensures the preparation and follow-up of key engagements including inter – institutional meetings, meetings with EU MS as well as internal EEAS matters. It coordinates senior management meetings, facilitates internal and external communication, and maintains day-to-day coordination with other EU institutions, Member States, and relevant external stakeholders. WE PROPOSE: The EEAS is launching a call for expression of interest for the recruitment of one ASSISTANT (AST2) as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of other servants of the EU in accordance with EEAS Decision Admin(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents. Please note that, candidates who have been engaged by the EEAS as non-permanent servants (temporary and contract agents engaged under Article 3b of the CEOS), will be bound by Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 14/07/2023 on the maximum duration of engagement by the European External Action Service of non-permanent staff under successive limited duration contracts of different types, and on the minimum lapse of time between successive contracts under Article 2(e) of the CEOS and repealing the Decision ADMIN(2020) 10 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 16/07/2020. WE LOOK FOR: A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she will be a critical member of the SG Office, working in an interesting and fast-paced context and will be entrusted with the following administrative tasks, to be carried out in close coordination with another Administrative Assistant: SG agenda & coordination Manage the Secretary-General’s diary, Outlook calendar, forward-planning, and contact lists; Screen incoming communication, filter telephone calls, and manage responses to general inquiries for the SG Office; Facilitate internal communication and coordination between the SG, EEAS Directorates, EU Institutions, and external interlocutors. Meetings & visitor management Organize internal and external meetings, events, and briefing files for the SG; Manage room bookings, submit visitor access requests, and welcome guests and official delegations. Mission & travel logistics Coordinate end-to-end travel logistics for the SG and SG Office, including itineraries, accommodation, visa arrangements, and liaison with Protocol; Support annual mission planning, track mission budgets, and process mission orders (MIPS) and reimbursement claims (ARES / representation costs). Workflow, correspondence & information security Contribute to monitoring incoming and outgoing correspondence in ARES, track deadlines, and manage the clearance workflow for briefings (e-brief); Maintain internal filing systems and shared drives, securely handling EU Classified Information (EUCI / RUE) according to security regulations. Office Operations & HR Support Liaise with EEAS support services for IT, equipment, furniture, telecom, and office supply procurement; Perform additional SG-level administrative tasks as required; Support HR administrative duties for the SG, including appraisal, promotion, selection, rotation/mobility, jobs descriptions, training plans and leave and absence management in Sysper2. LEGAL BASIS The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents The successful candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) at the grade of AST2. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Candidates must meet ALL of the following general and specific conditions on the closing date for online applications : Be a national of one of the EU Member States and enjoy full rights as a citizen; Meet any obligations imposed on him or her by the laws concerning military service; Provide the appropriate character references as to their suitability for the performance of their duties; Have the capacity to work in languages of the CFSP in writing and orally. Post-secondary education attested by a diploma followed by at least 3 years of relevant professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties OR secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, followed by at least 6 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents. In the case of applications from EU officials on leave for personal grounds, successful candidates will be reinstated into active employment within the meaning of Article 35(a) of the SR. SELECTION CRITERIA: Candidates should: Demonstrated strong capacity for organisation (be able to prioritise, plan, manage time, communicate clearly and concisely); Flexible, cooperative team player and able to multi-task and work autonomously; Ability to work under time pressure and to deal with urgent issues swiftly and independently; Sound computer skills (MS Office) and good knowledge of standard EU institutions IT workflow applications/ administrative procedures; Very good knowledge of written and verbal English, good knowledge of French (CFSP languages). Furthermore would be considered as assets. EXPRESSION OF INTEREST AND SELECTION PROCEDURE: The selection procedure will take place in three different and successive steps: 1. Expression of Interest Before submitting their application, candidates should carefully check whether they meet all the eligibility criteria in order to avoid exclusion from the selection procedure. Expressions of interest should be sent by e-mail to the following functional mailbox AST-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu For the purposes of the e-mail application, the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: "EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b-AST2-SG Office-job 469618" Such an expression of interest must be accompanied by: The deadline for submission of expressions is 20/10/2026 at 12:00 midday (Brussels time). For correspondence concerning the selection procedure, please use the following email address (the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b- AST2-SG Office-job 469618" ) : AST-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu 2. Pre-selection The selection panel will make a pre-selection on the basis of the qualifications and the professional experience described in the CV and motivation letter. 3. Selection The candidates who have passed the pre-selection step will be invited for an interview so that the selection panel can evaluate them objectively and impartially based on the selection criteria, as listed in the present call for expression of interest. Additional specific written or oral tests might be organised by the panel. Following a comparative assessment of the merits of the preselected candidates, the selection panel will recommend the name of a candidate to the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment, and possibly, name(s) of other candidate(s) that should be placed on a reserve list valid for maximum 12 months. That list would be used, on the one hand, in case of refusal of the offer or unavailability of the recommended candidate in the present procedure and/or, on the other hand, for other future similar recruitment needs. item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. No LC2026/03 The EUSR will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure by telephone. Please address any queries concerning this procedure or related to employment conditions and benefits to delegation-bosnia-and-herzegovina-eusr-personnel@eeas.europa.eu --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Note: Short-listed candidates will be asked to take an interview. Candidates who passed the interview will be invited for a testing. Deadline for application: 22 November 2026 at 23:59 hrs (Brussels time). Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted. Thank you for your interest. Terms of Reference Position Title: Driver Position reference number: LC 2026/03 Direct Supervisor: Head of Finance and Administration ( Salary grade: Grade V (Local Staff Salary Grid) Duty Station: Sarajevo Job Purpose The incumbent will provide safe, reliable and professional driving and related logistical support services to the EUSR team and official visitors, ensuring the proper use, maintenance and availability of assigned vehicles and appropriate reporting to the Head of Administration and Finance. The incumbent will report to the Head of Administration and Finance and Senior Procurement and Logistics Officer, through his/her assigned delegate, and will ensure consistent service delivery to the EUSR team. Typical Duties and Responsibilities Providing safe, reliable and professional driving services using a light-duty motor vehicle (passenger vehicle, light truck, small bus) on general assignments, in all types of weather conditions, within Bosnia and Herzegovina and to neighboring countries on official missions, to transport staff and visiting personnel; Professionally representing the EUSR BiH through responsible and safe driving, appropriate conduct and wearing the approved uniform; Supporting the day-to-day management of the EUSR vehicle fleet through regular physical and data checks; monitoring and anticipating maintenance, tyre replacement, insurance and vehicle registration requirements; consolidating fleet records; reporting anomalies or issues to both the SPLO and the HoFA together with proposed follow-up action; and preparing the procurement documentation required for fleet-related expenditure. Maintaining appearance of vehicles, inside at all times and outside when conditions permit; and performing minor vehicle maintenance and servicing within the limits of the driver's competence; Installing and removing tire chains as required by weather conditions Ensuring that required vehicle documentation, safety equipment and basic supplies are available and reporting any deficiencies to the supervisor; Maintaining vehicle log-books and records detailing official trips, daily mileage, petrol consumption, oil changes etc. Review, scanning for digital archive and filing hard copies of all vehicle logs. Immediately reporting accidents, incidents, vehicle breakdowns or other safety-related issues to the supervisor and completing the required reports in accordance with applicable EUSR procedures and local regulations: Receiving official visitors at the airport, clearly identifying themselves as representing the EUSR BiH, and facilitating immigration and customs formalities; Delivering or collecting documents, materials and light equipment; Coordinating daily driving assignments with the team and ensuring timely availability for scheduled journeys and official visitors; Ensuring compliance with applicable road safety requirements and EUSR procedures, including the appropriate use of seat belts and safe handling of official transportation; Performing other reasonable duties apparent or assigned to him/her. Professional Requirements/Qualifications Completed Secondary Education Minimum seven years' relevant professional experience, preferably including experience with an international organization, diplomatic mission or other multicultural working environment. Technical knowledge of professional driving and basic knowledge of vehicle mechanics. Ability to operate vehicle communication and other relevant communication equipment Good knowledge of routes throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina and familiarity with routes to neighbouring countries. Valid and clean driving license. Experience in driving 4x4 vehicles is essential, defense driving will be advantage. Basic First Aid knowledge. Good knowledge of local traffic laws. Ability to maintain simple records and complete relevant vehicle documentation. Good working knowledge of English and fluent knowledge of one of the official languages of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Availability to work outside regular working hours, including occasional weekends, public holidays and emergency assignments, when required by operational needs. Physical ability to lift and carry materials and light equipment. Competencies and Attributes Ability to take initiative and work in team setting with high sense of confidentiality and flexibility; Ability to operate independently and exercise sound judgement in the performance of assigned duties; Ability to operate within a fast-moving environment and react appropriately to change; ICT skills commensurate with the scope of the post. Very good interpersonal skills to interact within multicultural environment; General conditions The Candidate will need to be certified medically fit for employment by a competent authority/person in BiH. The successful candidate will be required to provide an official Certificate of Criminal Records issued by the competent authorities and hold a valid driving licence with a satisfactory driving history.

item.title: IT SUPPORT ASSISTANT
item.description: VACANCY NOTICE IT SUPPORT ASSISTANT LOCAL AGENT GROUP II Position 354912 – Administration Section We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the Democratic Republic of the Congo works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Democratic Republic of the Congo government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. The Delegation of the European Union to the Democratic Republic of the Congo primarily represents the institutions of the European Union in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and conducts political dialogue with the Congolese authorities and civil society to promote shared values and interests, including respect for human rights and political freedoms, the strengthening of democracy and the consolidation of the rule of law. We offer The post of Local IT Support Assistant. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. This is a full-time position (37.5 hours per week) for a Group II local agent, under an indefinite-term contract. The place of employment is the Delegation of the European Union to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Park Towers Building, 6th floor, at the intersection of Batetela and Ambassadeurs Avenues, Gombe, Kinshasa. Occasional atypical hours (evening, weekend), especially when asked to support the RITO or HQ Occasional travel for work missions Work is mainly performed in an office setting. However, it may very rarely involve the operation of heavy equipment (server room equipment such as rack UPS). Under this post, as an IT Assistant, the jobholder works under the supervision of the Head of Administration (HoA) and functional guidance received by the Regional IT Officer (RITO). The jobholder is responsible for providing a range of information technology support roles, including the delivery of end-user support and operational assistance to the RITO and to the EEAS IT HELPDESK (HQ). Interacts with all level of staff in the Delegation and Headquarters, as well as with external stakeholders to provide technical support services and to seek feedback to enhance systems. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: END-USER SUPPORT Prepare and setup IT hardware for newcomers (laptops, mobile phones), based on the HQ reference configuration. These processes use corporate provisioning mechanism and Mobile Device Management (MDM) software. Assist the end-users for office automation tools (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.) as well as other internal tools. Register user incidents into the ICT helpdesk system and ensure follow-up until their resolution. Install and test optional software and devices upon request by end-users. This can only be done in accordance with the applicable IT corporate guidelines defined by the EEAS. Support and train end-users to the use of presentation and videoconference equipment. Manage the stock of laptops and other accessories (screens, docking stations, keyboards, mouses, various cables, etc.) IT INFRASTRUCTURE Perform the troubleshooting of issues related to IT hardware (laptops, printers, projectors, telephones sets, etc.) Install updates and security patches on software or hardware equipment, in accordance with the instructions of HQ and RITO Setup and manage printers, scanners and “all-in-one” devices, and ensure their maintenance in accordance with the local service providers. Register issues with IT hardware delivered from HQ into the ICT helpdesk system and ensure follow-up and resolution Whenever necessary, perform the disk wiping for all declassified PC’s and decommission them from the inventory before submitting them to the HoA for donation. If required, manage the local PABX and telephones Act as the point of contact for HQ and for local IT/network service providers. Follow-up the hardware problems with ICT material delivered from HQ (laptops, PC’s and videoconference material) – opening – follow-up and closure of incidents with the helpdesk delegations ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT Assist the HoA with the preparation of call for tenders for the purchase of ICT material and/or IT related services based on specifications received by HQ. Assist the HoA and/or RITO in drafting technical requirements and, if necessary, in participating in the technical evaluation of possible options or offers. Assist with the inventory of the Delegation’s ICT equipment. Duties and responsibilities may be adapted according to the evolving needs of the European Union and its diplomatic representations. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 01/03/2027. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria Minimum of post-secondary degree or equivalent Post-secondary degree in Information Technology management or similar ( desirable ) Professional certifications in ICT field ( desirable ) Experience in a diplomatic mission, a development agency or in a multi-cultural international setting ( desirable ) Experience working with the European Union policies and procedures ( desirable ) Certificate of good conduct Enjoy civil rights and permits for employment Medically fit to perform the required duties Minimum of 5 years of professional experience as an IT officer, IT technician or similar; Working knowledge (B2) of English and French, and command of the local language(s). Right to residence and work in Democratic Republic of the Congo. Assets/selection criteria Command of the local language(s), command of the French language and working knowledge of English. Communicate effectively and clearly, both orally and in writing Knowledge of information technology and applications, including computer system networks Knowledge of system development workflow and document flow processes Ability to conduct network maintenance and to provide server services and user support Ability to conduct research and gather information from a wide variety of sources Proficient use of standard office information technology tools and systems BEHAVIOURAL ATTRIBUTES Ability to work in a multicultural team, showing good interpersonal skills Ability to adapt quickly and flexibly to new requests Capacity to focus on priorities, to show initiative and to organise own workload in order to respect deadlines Service-oriented mindset Eager to learn and develop new knowledge and competences High degree of integrity, confidentiality and responsibility How to apply The applicant must apply by sending A cover letter in French, signed A Curriculum Vitæ in French , using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/fr All documents to the following email address: eeasjobs-118@eeas.europa.eu Please indicate in the email subject line: Name – Position 354912 – Local IT Support Assistant Applications must be received no later than 19 November 2026 at 23:59. The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV, practical testing and interviews. item.title: Employment opportunity: Post of Project Officer for Private Sector Development and Investments at the EU Delegation to Pakistan in Islamabad, application deadline 22nd Nov 2026
item.description: The European Union Delegation to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Islamabad is looking for a: Project Manager for Private Sector Development and Investments We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Islamabad was established in Pakistan in 1985 with the objective of fostering closer and stronger ties between the EU and Pakistan, which expanded considerably since. The EU Delegation works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Pakistani government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. The EU is a major development cooperation partner of Pakistan, with a portfolio of close to EUR 100 million a year. EU-funded programmes and projects cover a wide range of sectors including rural development and economic growth, climate change and energy, education as well as governance and human rights. In addition, the EU has launched its Global Gateway Strategy. To meet global infrastructure development needs in line with the UN’s Agenda 2030 and its Sustainable Development Goals, its target is to mobilise between 2021 and 2027 up to EUR 300 billion of sustainable investments in quality infrastructure. We offer We are looking for a Project Manager for Private Sector Development and Investments (Local Agent Group 1) in the Delegation’s Partnership Section. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will, in close cooperation with and under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Rural Development and Economic Growth section, coordinate and monitor the implementation of ongoing projects in the field of economic growth, private sector development and investments, as well as in the formulation and advancement of new interventions in this field. In addition, we propose an interesting and diverse coordinating role supporting the roll out of the Global Gateway and the implementation of the Team Europe approach and initiatives. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: To advise on and manage projects and programs of development assistance and of financial and technical cooperation with third countries in the fields of economic growth, private sector development and investments; this involves in particular the management of a new programme to support export-oriented SMEs in Pakistan to become more competitive by better complying with evolving green legislation and standards from the EU; To support and contribute to policy dialogue with relevant public and private sector stakeholders in all areas of concern, with a special focus on infrastructure investments; Contribute and prepare inputs to briefings and Global Gateway horizontal issues; Maintain good and effective contacts with the local operators in the field, with the national authorities and institutions, with representatives of the diplomatic missions of the EU Member States as well as of European and International Financial Institutions, with representatives of the principal international donors, with NGOs and other local non-official actors; Prepare and assist in missions from Headquarters; Contribute to communication and visibility of programmes and ad hoc tasks relating to the activities of the Section and the Delegation. The job will be performed in a multicultural environment, based in Islamabad, with a working time of 37.5 hours per week. The team consists of 9 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. The annual base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 7,718,664 PKR. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 1 January 2027. The duration of the assignment is linked to the duration of the programme on SME competitiveness as outlined above. The duration is initially set for a period of 2 years which is aligned with the full roll-out of the challenge fund from the initial first call for proposals in the textiles in 2026, to the inclusion of all five of the target sectors in 2028. A next phase of the project (year 3) will be marked on the sequential disbursements of funds based on performance throughout 2029. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) A bachelor’s degree in (agricultural) economics, finance, business administration, public administration, international development, rural development, or similar relevant discipline;. Minimum 6 years professional experience (to be counted as from the qualifying degree), of which at least 3 years in an international organisation, or internationally funded projects; Minimum 3 years professional experience in finance or private sector development (which can be included in the overall 6 years of professional experience); Proven proficiency in understanding, speaking, reading and writing English. Ability to draft documents to high standard essential; High level of general IT literacy, in particular Microsoft Office (word, outlook, excel); Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned; Enjoys civil rights and permits for employment under local law; Have a clean criminal record (at the time of the recruitment). Assets / selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) a master’s degree in (agricultural) economics, finance, business administration, public administration, international development, rural development, or similar relevant discipline; Experience in project management, procurement and contract management; Strong knowledge of private sector development, access to finance, financial instruments, investment facilitation, and public-private partnerships; Knowledge of/ experience in international development cooperation; Knowledge of/ experience in EU development cooperation, in particular with relations to Global Gateway is considered a strong asset; Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills to engage with diverse stakeholders; Strong organisational and multitasking skills with the ability to manage complex tasks under pressure; A results-oriented approach as well as a highly developed ability to work as a part of a team. How to apply Please send your application and supporting documents exclusively by e-mail to eeasjobs-232@eeas.europa.eu ,, clearly mentioning in the subject: Application – post 113126– name of the applicant . The e-mail must include a cover letter, a detailed CV (preferably in Europass format) and copies of educational transcripts, degrees, experience letters referred to in the application. Applications that are not sent according to the above procedure will not be considered. The deadline for applications is : 22 nd November 2026 The successful candidate will be subject to medical check, background check, and others. The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. The Selection Committee will prepare a short-list of candidates who are considered to be the most suitable for the post on the basis of a preliminary assessment of the information provided in their application letter and the supporting documents. The short-listed candidates will be invited to an assessment phase, which may include a written test and an interview to assess the suitability of the candidates for the post. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will use the same means of publication as for this job advertisement to inform the remaining candidates once the recruitment procedure has been completed and that a candidate has (or has not) been recruited. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to eeasjobs-232@eeas.europa.eu , clearly mentioning in the subject: Request for information – post 113126 – name of the applicant . Requests that are not sent according to the above procedure will not be considered. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality and to preventing discrimination on any grounds. It actively welcomes applications from all qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential. If pre-selected, candidates with disabilities are invited to contact the Delegation eeasjobs-232@eeas.europa.eu , in order to accommodate any special needs and provide assistance to ensure equality of opportunities with other candidates. If a candidate with a disability is selected and recruited, the EEAS is committed to appropriate measures in order to accommodate his or her special needs to the working place or working conditions in accordance with Art 4 of the Decision ADMIN(2025)13 of the Director-General for Resource Management of the European External Action Service on providing reasonable accommodation for local staff with disabilities working in Union Delegations.

item.title: Administrative Agent - Contract Agent FGII - Job No 245682 - EEAS Headquarters - The Sanctions Division
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The Sanctions Division supports the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy and the High Representative through the development, adoption process and maintenance of restrictive measures (sanctions) in pursuit of specific foreign and security policy objectives. In particular: the Division coordinates and contributes to the design of sanctions, prepares and participates in discussions and negotiations regarding sanctions in the Council working groups, drives the process for the adoption of new measures and for the review of the 48 existing EU sanctions regimes, develops sanctions policy, prepares or supports the preparation of listings proposals, coordinates with likeminded countries where relevant, works on increased understanding of sanctions both inside the institutions and outside. The Division works very closely with many services within the EEAS, the Council and Commission in pursuing its mandate. The Sanctions Division is a growing team of 20 colleagues. WE PROPOSE The position of Administrative Agent contract agent FGII as per article 3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). The Administrative Agent will provide general administrative support to the Division, including document management, internal communication, organisation of meetings and missions, logistic needs and information provision. Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function group II), on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of one year that may be successively renewed up to a maximum duration of six years, subject to the maximum duration of engagement by the EEAS allowed under successive limited duration contracts of different types. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT ‎EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available: 1 February 2027 LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof. WE LOOK FOR A colleague motivated to join a two-person team providing the administrative support to the Sanctions Division. A dynamic, flexible and proactive colleague with good communication and organisational skills with a developed sense of service. The secretary should be able to quickly adapt to new working environment and be a good team-player. The successful candidate should have good computer skills, a sound knowledge of the standard IT applications and administrative procedures. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: provide efficient secretarial support; carry out various administrative tasks such as diary-keeping, filtering telephone calls, filing and ordering supplies, dealing with correspondence; document management: registration of incoming and outgoing correspondence, including in Ares; organise missions of staff using MIPS application; organise meetings and events; co-ordinate the creation, keeping up to date and retrieval of documents and data in the appropriate files or IT databases; ensure the preparation of briefing files, speeches, etc; coordinate and authorise translation requests. Eligibility criteria Further to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS, candidates must: have passed a valid EPSO CAST in a valid function group for this post, or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST in a valid function group for this post ( https://eu-careers.europa.eu/en/contract-staff-selection-procedures-always-open-registration ). In the latter case, while the registration will make the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the CAST exam; have a level of post-secondary education attested by a diploma or a level of secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education and appropriate professional experience of three year; have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties; be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen. Selection criteria Candidates should: have experience in the secretarial field; be well organised with the ability to deal with files in a timely manner; be a flexible and responsible team player with good inter-personal and communication skills; have good written and spoken English; have sound computer skills (MS Office) and good knowledge of standard administrative, workflow based IT applications and administrative procedures. Furthermore: experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; experience in working with or within other EU institutions; exposure to a secured environment; knowledge of other languages; experience/knowledge in the legal field; will be considered as strong assets. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality, of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks. In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest ( see attached ). MEDICAL CLEARANCE The signature of the contract will be subject to prior favourable opinion of the Medical Service, unless the successful candidate is a temporary agent currently employed in the EEAS. PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE (hereafter, “PSC”) The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC”) issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned. Candidates who do not already have a valid PSC will be required to go through the security clearance vetting procedure of their Member State to obtain this clearance in accordance with national laws and regulations and with the procedure laid down in the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 and in Annex A I of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . Until the PSC is issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned, the selected candidate will not be authorised to access EUCI at the level of CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL or above, or to participate in any meetings or workflow where EUCI is processed. Please note that the necessary procedure for obtaining a PSC can be initiated on request of the employer only, and not by the individual candidate. In case of failure to obtain or renew the required PSC, the AACC may take the appropriate measures in accordance with Article 7 of the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion. The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States. The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR. If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an email to CONTRACTAG

It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development assistance and engagement with multilateral organisations. As a fully-fledged diplomatic mission, the Delegation represents the European Union in its dealings with the Government of Rwanda across all areas within the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Administrative Assistant (Local Agent Group 2) in the Administration Section. The team consists of 10 people, and there are occasional atypical working hours. The successful candidate will work under the direct supervision and responsibility of the Head of Administration, provide expert support, operational assistance and specialist knowledge across a range of administrative functions. Specific responsibilities may be adjusted over time to reflect the evolving needs of the Delegation. The following main tasks and duties are currently required: Procurement and contract management Manage the full procurement life cycle for very low, low and middle value tenders, from needs identification through to contract signature, ensuring all procedures are conducted in strict compliance with applicable EU Financial Regulations and EEAS guidelines. Proactively monitor contract expiry dates and ensure that renewal or replacement tenders are initiated well in advance, avoiding any gap in service or operational disruption. Register all new contracts and order forms in the LCK application (contract management tool) and actively monitor contract consumption to ensure expenditure remains within authorised limits. Together with the Head of Administration, before the end of November each year, take the lead with the preparation and submitting a comprehensive forecast of tenders to be launched in the following calendar year. Register the annual procurement forecast in the PPMT application (procurement management tool) and monitor its implementation throughout the year. Budget / Finance Assist the Head of Admin and the Administration Accounts team in preparing the Delegation’s annual operating budget estimates in a timely manner. (Short-term training courses, certificates of attendance and professional development certificates do not, on their own, meet this educational requirement.) A minimum of 5 years of relevant, documented professional experience in administration, procurement, financial administration or a comparable administrative function, including practical experience in applying administrative procedures, maintaining records and working with financial or procurement documentation. Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in an international organisation or diplomatic mission. (may be included in the 5 years total). Very good computer skills (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Webex and MS Teams). Very good English level (English is the working language). Assets / selection criteria University degree in business administration, human resources, procurement, finance or any other field relevant to the tasks to be performed. item.title: National Training Experts / EU4Rivers Project
item.description: Curriculum Development and Training Delivery – EU Water Framework Directive The European Union (EU) has delegated the Austrian Development Agency (ADA) to implement the EU4Rivers Project in Albania. The Project supports the strengthening of institutional capacities for integrated water resources management and approximation with the EU water acquis, including implementation of the EU Water Framework Directive (WFD) and Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSDF). As an EU4Rivers initiative, with technical support from the University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU), and in support of the cooperation agreement between the Albanian Water Resources Management Agency (AMBU) and the Albanian School of Public Administration (ASPA), five mandatory training curricula will be developed and piloted during 2027. The aim is to establish a sustainable training programme for public administration personnel at both central and local levels whose roles and responsibilities are directly or indirectly linked to the implementation of the WFD in Albania, with regular courses offered through ASPA from 2028 onwards. EU4Rivers invites qualified experts to submit Expressions of Interest (EoIs) for the development of curricula and related training materials and delivery of pilot trainings. Interested experts may apply for one or more thematic areas. This is an open call; experts will be selected following an assessment of their suitability. Thematic areas and indicative requirements for experts THEMATIC AREA REQUIREMENTS FOR THE EXPERT NATURAL AND ANTHROPOGENIC PRESSURES ON SURFACE WATER AND GROUNDWATER Background in hydrology, hydrogeology, environmental sciences, engineering or a related field; demonstrable experience identifying and assessing natural and human pressures on water bodies, including WFD pressure/impact assessment. At least 7 years of relevant professional experience. EU WATER ACQUIS: LEGAL AND INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR IMPLEMENTATION IN ALBANIA Background in environmental or water law, public administration or a related field; experience with the Albanian water-governance framework, the EU WFD and related legislation, and their practical implementation. At least 7 years of relevant professional experience. RIVER BASIN MANAGEMENT PLANNING Background in water resources management, environmental planning or a related field; experience in river basin management planning, water-body characterisation, environmental objectives, programmes of measures and WFD planning processes. At least 7 years of relevant professional experience. WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY MONITORING Background in hydrology, hydrogeology, water quality, environmental sciences or engineering; experience in monitoring-network design, sampling, measurements, laboratory/field quality assurance, and interpretation of surface-water or groundwater monitoring results. At least 7 years of relevant professional experience. FROM DATA TO INFORMATION Background in environmental sciences, data management, statistics, water assessment, GIS or a related field; experience with validation, analysis, interpretation, reporting and communication of water monitoring data for management decisions. At least 7 years of relevant professional experience. Scope of engagement and indicative schedule With the support of BOKU experts, the selected national experts will: (i) develop curricula and training materials in Albanian and English, following ASPA curriculum methodology(ii) revise the materials after evaluation (if requested); (iii) participate in the mandatory ASPA Training of Trainers (ToT) and trainer-certification process; and (iv) deliver pilot training sessions, starting from July 2027 (indicative). From 2028 onwards, regular courses are expected to be delivered according to ASPA procedures. Future engagement is subject to institutional demand and the applicable trainer arrangements and is not guaranteed by selection under this call. Remuneration and engagement arrangements Experts selected for curriculum development and pilot delivery will be engaged through an agreement with BOKU University as part of the EU4Rivers Project. The length of each curriculum and the corresponding remuneration will be confirmed in the engagement arrangements. General requirements and application Applicants should demonstrate relevant academic qualifications and professional expertise in their chosen thematic area; familiarity with the WFD and the Albanian institutional context; experience in training, teaching or curriculum development; and the capacity to prepare materials in Albanian and English. Participation in both the January online ToT kick-off and the June 2027 ASPA ToT/certification process is mandatory. The EoI should include: an updated CV in English, a brief cover letter specifying the selected thematic area(s) and relevant experience in training/curriculum development, and confirmation of availability for the mandatory ToT and pilot-training activities. Submission: Please send the EoI to eu4rivers@ada.gv.at by November 24 th , 2026 with the subject “EoI – WFD Training Curricula – [Thematic Area]”. Expressions of Interest will be assessed on the basis of relevant qualifications, technical expertise, training experience and availability. Shortlisted candidates may be contacted for further information and, where applicable, invited to proceed with the relevant selection and engagement process. Submission of an EoI does not create an entitlement to selection or a contract. By submitting an EoI to ADA, applicants acknowledge the ADA Privacy Notice: www.entwicklung.at/en/media-centre/privacy-notice . Personal data will be handled in accordance with the applicable privacy notice and data-protection requirements. ADA will retain the personal data until the finalization of the EU4Rivers project, which is currently planned for 30.09.2028.

The EU Delegation to the Republic of Moldova works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the authorities of the Republic of Moldova in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. We offer The post of Trade Officer (Local Agent Job Profile of Policy officer (incl. Trade Affairs officer), Group I) in the Delegation’s Cooperation Section, in close cooperation with the Political, Press and Information Section, under an indefinite employment contract. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of Cooperation Section, and in close cooperation with the Head of the Political, Press and Information section and other DG Trade staff present in the Delegation, providing support, expertise and assistance in trade, macroeconomic development, business environment, market access, TBT (Technical Barriers to Trade); export promotion/investment attraction, and related areas. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: POLICY DEVELOPMENT To support the activities aimed at improving business climate in Moldova and increasing business opportunities, for both Moldovan and EU economic operators; Contribute to removal of trade barriers and business constraints, in close consultation with Relevant Commission, EEAS and Member State representatives. Compile in a list, process and follow up on trade barriers and complaints from the EU economic operators. Structure the data and prepare lines to take proposals for the decision making. Contribute to preparing, assisting and follow-up on missions of DG TRADE, ECFIN and other relevant DG's and EU institutions. Contribute to preparing, assisting and follow-up of relevant policy dialogue meetings such as the Association Committee in Trade Configuration and other relevant Sub-committee meetings. EXTERNAL COMMUNICATION (general) Assist the dialogue with all relevant Governmental authorities, business organizations, agencies, civil society organizations, international partners and other relevant stakeholders in all areas of concern. Communication and outreach activities: presentation of EU activities to wider public Exchange information with Member States and co-ordinate possible joint actions; demarches, interface with IFI's, EU MS and other like-minded partners under the Team Europe approach; Contribute to communication activities and events by giving presentations and providing written input to newsletters, reports etc. and contribute contents related to trade and economy to Delegation webpage, trade webpage and relevant social media of the Delegation. POLICY ANALYSIS Collect and process information from relevant sources on business environment and market access. Monitor, analyses and report economic and trade related developments in the Transnistria region. Contribute to drafting of the Enlargement Report and other strategic documents. Contribute to sector analysis and to the identification of the financing priorities under the financial assistance programming exercise. INTERNAL COMMUNICATION (general) Draft policy notes, briefings, speeches lines to take and other documents, and carry out policy and other horizontal work in the field of trade policy and economy. Assist the HoD in explaining the EU and the Euro economic policies, inform the public of developments in macro-economic developments and governance inside the EU and the Euro area. Providing occasional linguistic support. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 2797 EUR. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be tentatively 1 March 2027. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) High education Degree in Economics, Law or International Relations; At least 3 years of experience in business, finance, economics, law, or related fields. The professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. Language Proficiency: An excellent command of Romanian (C2 level) , very good command of English (minimum C1 level) and good command of Russian (preferably C1 level); Knowledge of IT tools: Microsoft office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Zoom), Microsoft Teams, Webex; This post is a local-agent post. Applicants must have a valid work and residence permits; Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned. Assets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) How to apply The applicant must apply by sending a cover letter in English a Curriculum Vitæ (to include, at the minimum, exact job titles, employer’s name and detailed tasks descriptions) using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/en all documents to the following email address: eeasjobs-161@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email’ subject: “ Ref: 199543 – JOB TITLE: Trade Officer “ no later than 20/12/2026 by 18:00h local time. Late applications will not be accepted. Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares r relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV; practical testing and interviews. The best candidates will be invited to the final interview and a possible written test. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration. The successful candidate will be subject to a medical check. Candidates who wish to lodge a complaint regarding the recruitment process may submit a written communication to the functional mailbox to which they sent the initial application. Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, where appropriate, consult Headquarters before providing a response. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality, preventing discrimination on any grounds and ensuring a zero tolerance approach to any form of harassment. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential. item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. GLOBAL GI.1 Division aims to ensure that the design and implementation of the EU's broad range of economic and health-related policies are coherent with and support the EU's foreign policy and external initiatives. Key policy areas include economic security, trade, supply chain resilience, fiscal and financial policies, and global health as well as the coordination of the EEAS contribution to G20. The Division is also the focal point for the OECD and BRICS format. The Division has a highly motivated team with each member working flexibly with all colleagues, including from other divisions across the EEAS as well as stakeholders across the institutions, including Commission and Council. GLOBAL.GI.5 Division has a double mission of (i) overseeing the preparation, programming, implementation and review of the multiannual financial framework, and (ii) contributing to the implementation of 2030 Agenda and related EU objectives. Institutionally, GLOBAL.GI.5 Division supports the HRVP as chair of the FAC in Development Ministers formation and for her participation in the High-Level Geopolitical Dialogue on NDICI-Global Europe with the European Parliament. The Division is also the focal point for development related meetings at the Council (CODEV-PI) and the EP (DEVE). item.title: Secretary - Local Agent Group 3
item.description: We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership of 27 European countries. Abroad, the EU is represented through a network of over 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations. EU Delegations are fully-fledged diplomatic Missions working under the authority of an EU Ambassador / Head of Delegation. EU Delegations represent the Union in the country, promote cooperation in areas of shared interest, and proactively communicate to local audiences on EU matters. They work in close coordination with the Embassies of the 27 EU Member States. We offer The EU Delegation to New Zealand, based in Wellington, has a staff of 12. We are offering a full-time position of Secretary (Local Agent Group 3) assigned the Section of the Head of Delegation. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision of the Head of Delegation, providing general administrative and logistic support to the Ambassador as well as to other members of the Mission. The main responsibilities are listed below, and may be adjusted to meet the future needs of the Delegation: Administrative and logistical support to the Head of Delegation and to other members of the Missions. Scheduling of meetings and official engagements, answering telephone calls.. Preparation and transmission of administrative notes and reports. Handling correspondence, replying to invitations. Communication with New Zealand interlocutors, diplomatic Missions, and other stakeholders. Preparing and organizing missions (planning, authorisations, reservations, programmes, processing of reimbursements). Logistics for receptions, meetings, conferences. Assistance with HR- related tasks Preparing and participating in public outreach and communication activities and events. Logistical and secretarial support to high-level visits arriving from EU Headquarters. Managing the Delegation’s contacts database, under the guidance of the Delegation Data Protection correspondent. Other administrative and clerical tasks, as required. Back-up for the Assistant to the Ambassador. The exact base salary will be calculated based on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 5521 NZD/month. The position offers a competitive benefits package (subject to specific conditions), health insurance and a retirement savings plan. The position may occasionally require atypical working hours. Expected start date: as soon as possible. Minimum requirements and eligibility criteria (essential for the application to be considered): The candidate must be: i) a New Zealand citizen, or ii) a holder of a valid residency visa authorizing to reside and work full time in New Zealand, currently residing in New Zealand; Education: Minimum high school leaving certificate; Professional experience: Minimum of 2 years of experience in an administrative or secretarial role, office management or similar. This professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. Language skills: Excellent command of English (C1), orally and in writing. Computer Literacy: excellent knowledge of MS Office tools and the ability to use other administrative software and applications. Additional assets considered in the selection process: Further education in fields related to the role (such as administration, management, international relations) Proven work experience in a diplomatic Mission, in government or an international organisation; Proficiency in additional EU languages, and/or te reo Māori; Knowledge of internal software or applications such as ARES, MIPS+ and other EU applications The ideal candidate will be: A fast learner ready to embrace new challenges A strong communicator Able to work in an autonomous manner A good team player, respectful of the Delegation’s international and multicultural team How to apply The applicant must apply by sending Please send your application package above in PDF format to the following email address: eeasjobs-162@eeas.europa.eu And mention in the email subject: “ Ref: 5234427– JOB TITLE: Secretary “ The deadline for the submission of applications is: Friday 18 December 2026 at 18:00 New Zealand Standard Time (NZST) (UTC+12:00). Applications submitted in a format other than PDF , sent via any means other than the specified email address , or received after the deadline indicated above will not be taken into consideration . Caution: The applicant must verify that he/she fulfils all the conditions. For easy verification, the applicant must mark all the squares relating to each document or application condition. The absence of one of these conditions or documents is a reason for the rejection of the application. The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to selection by a committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, in addition to CV screening and an interview, the selection Committee may decide to include additional steps (such as an in-tray exercise or another form of practical testing). Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to the Delegation’s Administration via the functional mailbox to which the initial application was sent. The successful candidate will be offered an open term contract starting in January 2026 (tentative date), following a probationary period of 3 months (90 days). The successful candidate will be required, as a condition of the offer of employment, to provide all supporting documents in regards of diplomas and professional experience as declared in the application form, will be subject to a pre-employment medical examination and provide a medical fitness certificate confirming their fitness to carry out the assigned duties, and a clean criminal record. Candidates who wish to lodge a complaint regarding the recruitment process may submit a written communication to the functional mailbox to which they sent the initial application. Upon receipt, the Delegation will review the matter and, where appropriate, consult Headquarters before providing a response.
